findings.claim: The genuine gift-and-borrow heter for the needed Shabbos utensil is retained.
findings.evidence: YD 120:16 expressly permits the gift and subsequent borrowing when immersion was forgotten before Shabbos or Yom Tov; OC 323:7 gives this route amid the immersion-on-Shabbos dispute. MB 323:34 expressly permits this gift for the Shabbos need.

findings.claim: No-effective-transfer counterfactual correctly changes the result.
findings.evidence: YD 120:8 exempts borrowing from non-Jewish ownership but retains the obligation on a utensil acquired by a Jew, including when lent onward. Together with the gift requirement in 120:16, this supports the answer’s distinction between ownership and mere temporary possession. Peninei Halakhah likewise bases the exemption on continuing non-Jewish ownership.
findings.locator: YD 120:8,16; Peninei Halakhah Kashrut 31:7, first and subsequent body paragraphs

findings.claim: Actual Jewish reacquisition and continuing borrowing are correctly separated.
findings.evidence: YD 120:11 requires immersion after sale and reacquisition; 120:3 supplies the blessing rule. Peninei Halakhah explicitly recommends a gift back after Shabbos and immersion with a blessing. Taz 120:18 and MB 323:35 require later immersion for permanent retention even without an express repurchase, with the stated blessing precaution.
findings.locator: YD 120:3,11; Taz YD 120:18; MB 323:35; Peninei Halakhah Kashrut 31:7, body paragraph on gift-and-loan

findings.claim: Routine avoidance when immersion is available is not presented as the ordinary ruling.
findings.evidence: The Rema’s weekday extension in YD 120:16 names absence of a mikveh; Arukh HaShulchan 120:60 limits the arrangement until after Shabbos or access to a mikveh, then requires immersion without a blessing. This agrees with the scope of the target Hidabroot answer, although the candidate cites the underlying sources rather than that page.
findings.locator: Rema YD 120:16; Arukh HaShulchan YD 120:60; Hidabroot answer paragraphs 1–2

findings.claim: The contemporary continuing-loan leniency is accurately represented as a distinct position.
findings.evidence: Rav Melamed explicitly rules that intention never to acquire prevents involuntary acquisition and permits continuing use under non-Jewish ownership. His note 10 discusses the Taz/MB position and contrasts the lenient authorities and reasoning. The answer reports this permission and its ownership condition while retaining his recommendation to reacquire and immerse.
findings.locator: Peninei Halakhah Kashrut 31:7, body paragraphs 2–4 and note 10

findings.claim: The ha’aramah objection and its evidentiary limit are honestly attributed.
findings.evidence: Pitchei Teshuvah 120:15 reports Rashbash 468 as questioning the arrangement as ha’aramah. The answer says it verified that report but not the full responsum; it does not turn the reported objection into a unanimous rejection.

The quoted Hebrew in YD 120:16 and MB 323:34 matches. All substantive cited locators inspected resolve to supporting passages. No material unsupported categorical claim found within the stipulated case.

findings.claim: The phrase “remains nominally on loan” could be clearer.
findings.evidence: Because the answer previously rejects an ineffective gift, “remains on loan but will be permanently retained” would describe the Taz/MB branch more cleanly. This is a wording issue, not a substantive loss of the ownership distinction.

limits: AI source review, not an expert halachic determination or practical psak.
I independently inspected the target Hidabroot answer, the exact Shulchan Arukh and Mishnah Berurah passages, Taz, Pitchei Teshuvah, Arukh HaShulchan, and Peninei Halakhah 31:7 including note 10.
I did not independently inspect the full Rashbash responsum or all authorities cited inside Peninei Halakhah’s footnote. The candidate also expressly discloses its Rashbash gap.
No transaction was assessed: effective transfer and a definitely obligated metal food utensil are the stipulated facts. The review does not validate a particular kinyan or appliance.
